steps.title: One park, two moods
paragraphs: Sunlight spilled across the grass. Ducks paddled lazily, a dog chased a frisbee, and somewhere an ice-cream van jingled.
Fog hung over the grass. The swings creaked, though no one was on them, and the pond lay black and still.
Same park. Same pond. But the first one feels bright and safe, and the second feels gloomy and tense. The writer chose the details that build each mood.

cards.title: Mood
cards.body: Mood is the feeling a place gives the reader: calm or tense, bright or gloomy, safe or dangerous. You build mood with your choice of details: the light, the weather, the sounds, and the objects you notice.

cards.title: Name it or build it
cards.showing: The front door hung from one hinge, and something inside dripped, slow and steady, in the dark.
cards.note: The second version never says "scary". The broken door, the drip and the dark do the work.

cards.title: Your mood toolkit
cards.body: Light: golden sun or dim shadows? Weather: a soft breeze or a storm? Sounds: birdsong or a sudden crack? Sentences: long and flowing for calm, short and sharp for tense.

cards.title: Find the mood words
cards.prompt: Tap the three words that make this attic feel gloomy.
cards.text: Dust covered the boxes, cobwebs drooped from the beams, and one dim bulb flickered.

prompts: Which detail builds your mood the most? Why?
Did Quill's reader feel the mood you chose? What would you change?
